robustness.description: AMCE instead of MM (cregg amce, by sector, baseline '1 Adult'); primary AMCE of '2 Adults, 3 Childr.' for Private Sector; secondary cj_anova omnibus test of sector differences
robustness.note: Secondary omnibus cj_anova by sector: F = 2.060697, p = 0.001385; pre-registered rule (p >= .05 = no difference, as the paper) gives same_as_paper = False. cregg's cj_anova is an unclustered nested-model F test, and pooled_df2 carries the duplicated rows described under bugs, so this p-value treats rows as independent.

bugs.description: left_join(pooled_df2, ebalw) duplicates rows: ebalw comes from match_data filtered to task == 1 (line 92), which has 2 rows (profiles) per respondent, so every matched civic respondent's 16 rows become 32. pooled_df2 is overwritten by this join and is the input of every cj() call in 04_analysis.R (Figures 1-4, A3, A4), and match_cj (Figure A2) inherits the duplication.
bugs.evidence: dplyr warns 'Detected an unexpected many-to-many relationship' (outputs/run_authors_warnings.txt). outputs/code_checks.json: 87936 rows vs 62112 distinct (respondent, task, profile); 1614 respondents have 32 rows. Rerunning Figure 1/2 cj() on de-duplicated rows changes MMs by at most 0.000900329929226951 and SEs by at most 0.40% relative; FC1 count stays 0 (outputs/code_check_dedup_fig1_mm.csv, code_check_dedup_fig2_mmdiff.csv). Respondents with an NA balance covariate (na.omit, line 122) keep 16 rows, so they get half the weight of others.

PREREG risk section expected the general-population counts might match the appendix (1336 / 352 / 1937); they match Table 2 instead (1285 / 333). The 88 civic respondents absent from survey_data.csv equal footnote 5's 88 non-German respondents in number; that they are the same people is not verifiable from the deposit.

In survey_data.csv, for civic respondents v184_ger is 'Ja' for exactly the 333 Public Sector respondents and 'Nein' for exactly the 1285 Private Sector ones (outputs/t3_sector_by_v184_ger.csv). 03 line 98 names v184_ger == 'Ja' 'nongerman'. If v184_ger were nationality this cross-tab would be unexpected; the variable is not documented in the deposit and nongerman is not used in any balance or estimate, so this is an unverified observation with no effect on results.

FC1 holds (0 of the FC1 levels), but 2 Duration-of-unemployment levels ('1 Year', '3 Years') have mm_diff CIs excluding 0 (outputs/figure_claims.json), as visible in the published Figure 2; the text makes no claim about duration.

R_c secondary: cj_anova by sector gives p < .05 (see robustness note); that test ignores respondent clustering and runs on the duplicated rows, so it is likely anti-conservative. Robustness does not change the class.
